$comment: Golden cases for the amount-in-words line on an Indian invoice. The word sequences in `numbers` and the numeric part of `cases` come from num2words(lang='en_IN'), normalised: no hyphens, no connective 'and', Title Case. The framing around them — the rupee word, the paise tail, 'Only' — is the one documented on TaxRegime.amountInWords. Changing either the grouping or the framing must fail here.

cases.words: Rupees One Thousand Two Hundred Thirty Four and Fifty Paise Only
cases.why: the example written on the TaxRegime contract, verbatim
nil, and still plural
singular — the only count that takes it
trailing zeros do not make it plural
the other side of the singular boundary

cases.words: Rupee One and One Paisa Only
cases.why: both singulars at once — one rupee, one paisa
the teens are single words
no hyphen — num2words writes twenty-one, the convention here does not
forty, not fourty
no connective 'and' before the units

Rupees One Thousand Two Hundred Thirty Four Only
Rupees Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Nine Only
Rupees Nineteen Thousand Ninety Two Only
Rupees Ninety Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Nine Only

cases.why: the lakh boundary — a western grouping would say one hundred thousand
one rupee past a lakh is still plural rupees
lakh does not pluralise

cases.words: Rupees Nine Lakh Ninety Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Nine Only

cases.why: a million is ten lakh, not one of anything

cases.words: Rupees Twelve Lakh Thirty Four Thousand Five Hundred Sixty Seven Only

cases.why: exactly on the tie — half-up, so it becomes a paisa

cases.words: Rupees Zero and One Paisa Only
Rupees Zero and Two Paise Only

and over the ten-lakh boundary
and over the crore boundary — the carry has to propagate through three groups
